I found one likely bug in the uncommitted change to `rich/panel.py`. I haven't run it, so this comes from reading the code.

**`rich/panel.py:204` and `rich/panel.py:253`: the title and subtitle lose the panel's `style`.**

The change styles the title and subtitle with `partial_border_style`, which is only `border_style` and no longer includes `self.style`. Everything around the title still uses the combined `border_style`:
- `align_text(..., border_style)` at lines 233–239 pads the title with the combined style.
- The top-left and top-right corner segments at lines 240 and 242 use it too.
- The `console.render(title_text, ...)` calls don't pass `style=`, so the title text never picks up the panel `style` from anywhere else.

For example, take `Panel("x", title="T", style="white on blue", border_style="red")`. Before the change, the title was `white on blue` plus `red`. Now it is just `red` with no background, so the title text appears as a gap in the panel's background colour. The same happens to the subtitle on the bottom border.

If the intent was to stop the panel's foreground colour overriding the title's own styling, the title text still needs the panel's background. For example, render it with `style=style`, or only strip the foreground.
